builder_bold.label: The Believer
builder_bold.identity: Everything you make goes back into what you're creating. You'd rather bet big on yourself than hold back and wonder what you left on the table.
builder_bold.driver: To build something whose value is undeniable, proof that betting everything on yourself was the right call.
strengthBullets: Conviction in what you are building
builder_bold.strengthBody: You are willing to put real effort behind an idea you believe in. That can be useful when it has a clear purpose and boundaries.
builder_bold.pitfallHead: Everything can become one big bet.
builder_bold.pitfallBody: When most of your time and money depend on the same source, a setback there can spill into the rest of your life. Building outside it deserves a place in the plan.

next.label: Set a real target
next.text: Work with your team to define what financial freedom actually looks like for you, so decisions get made strategically instead of emotionally.

next.label: Build beyond your main income source
next.text: Once you have accounted for your needs and reserves, explore how to build wealth outside the work that currently pays you.

builder_cautious.label: The Architect
builder_cautious.identity: You are a patient builder, intent on creating something of value but also aware of the cost if something were to go wrong.
builder_cautious.driver: To get where you want to go without losing it all.
builder_cautious.strengthBody: You tend to think through what could go wrong before committing. That can help you make deliberate choices.
builder_cautious.pitfallHead: The discipline can quietly become a ceiling.
builder_cautious.pitfallBody: Waiting for complete certainty can leave a good next step permanently on hold. The question is which risks fit the goal, and which do not.

next.text: Work with your team to define what financial freedom actually looks like for you, so decisions get made strategically instead of emotionally.

accumulator_bold.label: The Accelerator
accumulator_bold.identity: More money is coming in, and you see possibilities everywhere. Your instinct is to put it to work rather than leave it sitting without a purpose.
accumulator_bold.driver: To know every dollar coming in is being put to its best use immediately.
accumulator_bold.strengthBody: You are open to possibilities and willing to evaluate a new path. A clear filter can help that energy serve the bigger picture.
accumulator_bold.pitfallHead: Finding opportunity is just the first half of the battle.
accumulator_bold.pitfallBody: Each opportunity can sound reasonable on its own. Without a coordinated plan, the collection can bring more complexity, concentration and commitments than you intended.

next.label: Put a filter around opportunities
next.text: Decide what an opportunity needs to do for you before evaluating it. Bring the people you trust into decisions that deserve a second perspective.

next.label: Get one coordinated strategy in place
next.text: Find a team that can help you evaluate and orient the scattered positions you already have before adding the next one.

accumulator_cautious.label: The Banker
accumulator_cautious.identity: Your income is outpacing your spending, and it's creating real margin. It's likely that margin ends up just sitting in the bank, because there's never really been a plan for what to do with it.
accumulator_cautious.driver: To make sure you never go backwards, each win adding to the previous and creating additional security.
strengthBullets: Money available for a deliberate next step
accumulator_cautious.strengthBody: Having cash available can give you options. The useful next question is how much needs to stay ready and what the rest is meant to do.
accumulator_cautious.pitfallHead: Safety can quietly become standing still.
accumulator_cautious.pitfallBody: Cash has a job, but keeping every dollar there indefinitely can create its own tradeoffs, including inflation and missed opportunities. A clear cash target helps separate reserves from money for longer-term goals.

next.label: Give your cash a number
next.text: Account for spending, taxes, upcoming commitments and an appropriate reserve. Decide what needs to stay available before investing anything else.

next.label: Organize the rest by when you need it
next.text: Connect your accounts and investments to Today, Tomorrow and Beyond. Compare costs, access and risk before making a move.

navigator_bold.label: The Pioneer
navigator_bold.identity: You're in the middle of a major transition and have big money decisions to make. Your first instinct is to move, deploy, act, as the cost of missing out on growth feels more significant than the risk of making a bad decision.
navigator_bold.driver: To be moving forward, pursuing the new thing while trusting your talents and abilities.
navigator_bold.strengthBody: You are willing to take action when life changes. Pair that energy with enough time to understand the options.
navigator_bold.pitfallHead: A new chapter deserves a fresh plan.
navigator_bold.pitfallBody: The instincts that worked in the last stage may not fit this one. Before committing, understand deadlines, taxes and what would be difficult to undo.

next.label: Separate urgent from important
next.text: Handle real deadlines first. Give major choices a deliberate review window that fits the situation, rather than rushing or ignoring a deadline.

next.label: Get everyone in the same conversation
next.text: Coordinate the people advising you before assets move or commitments are made. Compare more than one path.

navigator_cautious.label: The Guardian
navigator_cautious.identity: You're in the middle of a major transition and have big money decisions to make. Your instinct is to protect and wait, often meaning the money sits entirely in cash while you “figure it out.”
navigator_cautious.driver: To protect what took this long to build, long enough to be certain the next move is actually the right one.
strengthBullets: Respect for what you have built
navigator_cautious.strengthBody: A pause can create room to think clearly. It works best when you also know what needs attention and when.
navigator_cautious.pitfallHead: “Figuring it out” can quietly become permanent.
navigator_cautious.pitfallBody: A temporary pause can become years without a decision. Keeping money available may be appropriate now, but it still needs a purpose and a review date.

next.label: Name the next decision
next.text: Work with your team to understand the choices, deadlines and tradeoffs. Set a review date so the pause has a purpose.

next.label: Build in stages
next.text: You do not have to move everything at once. Separate near-term needs from money with more time, then take deliberate steps.

steward.label: The Benefactor
steward.identity: You are thinking beyond yourself: family, community and the causes you care about. What your money can make possible matters as much as the balance.
steward.driver: To maximize the external potential of everything you've built.
steward.strengthBody: Knowing who and what you care about gives the plan direction. Your own foundation still matters, even when helping others is the priority.
steward.pitfallBody: Good intentions need a workable structure. Giving without checking your own needs, or keeping a family plan to yourself, can undermine the impact you want to make.
